# Engine drift fixtures

Seventeen JSON files, each a list of cases `{"name", "input", "expected"}`. The first eight (`adjust`, `fcpi`, `changes`, `forecast`, `scenario`, `procure`, `ask`, `xray`) are the price and lab engines; the next eight (`pressure`, `effective_supply`, `exposure`, `anomalies`, `infra_scenario`, `evaluation`, `signals`, `assistant`) are the inferred-state layer of architecture §10. The seventeenth, `evaluation_terminal`, pins a composition rather than an engine: the full evaluation payload the route builds for two tickers over the sample bag with no live source answering (terminal.py `_evaluate_ticker_uncached`), so the route-handler tier must feed the harness exactly the same closes, feature series, fallbacks and feed and report the same verdicts. `input` is JSON-native (camelCase keys, ISO 8601 `Z` datetimes, `[iso, value]` point pairs, a `series` map of id to `{unit, kind, points}`, no NaN) and `expected` is exactly what the Python engine returned for it, with floats the engine does not itself round frozen to six decimals (a port compares with that tolerance); a refusal is `{"error": "<flopx code>", "details": {...}}` or `{"error": "value-error", "message": "..."}`. Cases are built from the sample data under `product/flopx/data/sample/` plus hand-chosen edges (empty and single offer sets, an empty pressure cell, a facility with no date, a cell with three asks that must not report dispersion, an anomaly with no documented exposure, a series too short to evaluate, a mixed live and sample set that must be refused). Time-dependent fields are fixed in the input (`now`, `asOf`) or left out of the expected value (`fetchedAt`), so every case is deterministic. The pressure fixture's `sample-grid-all-cells` case carries every sample offer, facility, market and feed item the engine reads, so a port can reproduce the whole grid; the anomaly and signal fixtures take precomputed cells as input (scores and factor numbers only) so the detector can be tested apart from the index. Size limits are per file (`SIZE_LIMIT_KB` in `export.py`; 60 KB unless listed). Regenerate from `fastapi_backend/` with `.venv/bin/python product/flopx/tests/fixtures/engine/export.py`; `--check` exits 1 when any file would change, and `product/flopx/tests/test_engine_fixtures.py` re-runs every case through the engine so the files cannot drift from the Python. A TypeScript port copies these files verbatim and runs the same cases through its own engine.
